Historically unknown|cadet branches=|surname nihongo=大神|surname=Miwa|image=三本杉紋.jpg|parent house=[[Kamo clan]]}}{{Infobox Japanese clan | name = Miwa clan → Ōmiwa clan | image = [[File:三本杉（さんぼんすぎ）.png|250px]]
Representative crest: Three Cedars (Sanbon-sugi) | home_province = Yamato Province | titles = Kimi
Ōmiwa Kimi → later Ōmiwa Asomi | founder = Ōhiko
(descendant of Ōmononushi) | current_head = | founding_year = | dissolution = | cadet_branches = Yamanoi family (Chikage)
Fujibayashi family (Chikage)
Ōtsu family (Chikage)
Takamiyagawa family (Shakage)
Tsutsui clan (Warrior clan)
Anan clan (Warrior clan)
Tajiri clan (Warrior clan)
Mitsuyoshi clan (Warrior clan)
Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[samurai]] family who have served the [[Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[Asuka period]]. During the [[Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Isonokami clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[Silla]]. In the second year of [[Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. Miwa] ]] ]] == Related topics == * [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] * [[Ōtataneko]] * [[Kamo no Asomi clan]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Citation|author=坂本太郎・家永三郎・井上光貞・大野晋|title=[[Nihon Shoki]]|publisher=岩波書店|year=1994}} * {{Citation|author=倉野憲司|title=[[古事記]]|publisher=岩波書店|series=岩波文庫|year=1963}} * {{Citation|author=岩沢愿彦|title=[[系図纂要]]|publisher=名著出版|year=1997}} * {{Cite book|author=太田亮|editor=上田萬年・三上参次|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id=47004572|volume=1|chapter=大神　オホミワ|pages=1308-1313|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1130845/728|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070}} * {{Cite book|author=佐伯有清|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=雄山閣出版|year=1994}} * {{Cite book|author=坂本太郎・平野邦雄|title=日本古代氏族人名辞典|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=1990}} * {{Cite book|author=宝賀寿男|title=古代氏族の研究⑦　三輪氏 大物主神の祭祀者|publisher=青垣出版|year=2015}} * {{Cite journal|author=村島秀次|title=「大物主神 = 事代主神」論|journal=歴史研究|issue=618|year=2014}} * {{Cite journal|author=豊永聡美|title=大神景光-後醍醐・光明天皇の御笛師-|journal=日本音楽史研究|issue=5|year=2004}} (reprinted in {{Cite book|title=中世の天皇と音楽|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=2006|isbn=4642028609}}) * {{Cite web|author=おとくにフォトカルチャーラボ|title=三輪氏考|url=http://ek1010.sakura.ne.jp/1234-7-16.html|accessdate=2023-06-12}} * {{citation needed|Ōmiwa clan}} {{Suwa Faith}}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{citation needed|Miwa clan}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Miwa clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Miwa clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:japanese clans]] }} [[en:Miwa clan]] [[ja:大神氏]] [[sn:Miwa clan]] [[sn:iwa clan]] [[ja:Miwa clan]] [[Category:Ambox transclusions]]

{{Otheruseslist|[[大和国]]の「おおみわ」氏|[[豊後国]]の「おおが」氏|大神氏 (豊後国)}} {{日本の氏族 (古代氏族) |氏名 = 三輪氏 → 大三輪氏 |画像 = [[File:三本杉（さんぼんすぎ）.png|250px]]
[[家紋|代表紋]]：三本杉（さんぼんすぎ） |氏姓 = 三輪[[君 (カバネ)|君]]
大三輪君 → のち大三輪[[朝臣]] |始祖 = [[大田田根子]]
（[[大物主|大物主神]]後裔） |出自 = |氏祖 = [[大三輪大友主]]（大友主命） |種別 = [[神別]]（[[天津神・国津神#国津神|地祇]]） |本貫 = [[大和国]][[式上郡|城上郡]]大神郷 |人物 = [[三輪逆]]
[[三輪子首]]
[[三輪高市麻呂]] |後裔 = 山井家（[[地下家]]）
[[藤林家]]（地下家）
[[大津家]]（地下家）
[[高宮家]]（[[社家]]）
[[筒井氏]]（[[武家]]）
[[阿南氏]]（武家)

[[光吉氏]]（武家）
[[稙田氏]]（武家） など }} '''大三輪氏'''（おおみわうじ）、または'''三輪氏'''（みわうじ）は、[[大和国]][[磯城]]を発祥とし、[[大物主神]]を[[祖神]]とする[[氏族]]。 == 概要 == 直接的には、大田田根子の孫・[[大三輪大友主]]が氏祖である。 [[大神神社]]（[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]三輪）を奉斎する大和国磯城地方（のちの大和国[[式上郡|城上郡]]・[[式下郡|城下郡]]、現在の[[奈良県]][[磯城郡]]の大部分と[[天理市]]南部及び[[桜井市]]西北部などを含む一帯）が[[本貫]]。 氏の名は大和国城上郡大神郷の[[地名]]に[[発祥|由来]]する。三輪氏の[[カバネ|姓]]は初め'''[[キミ (カバネ)|君]]'''だったが、[[天武天皇]]13年（[[684年]]）11月に[[三輪高市麻呂]]ら一族が[[朝臣]]姓を賜り[[#otokuni|三輪氏考]]、改賜姓五十二氏の筆頭となる。[[飛鳥時代]]の後半期の[[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]では、氏族として最高位にあったとする。[[奈良時代]]には多くが三輪氏と名乗るようになる[[#kodai|『日本古代氏族事典』]]。 同族に[[賀茂朝臣氏|鴨君]]、神部直、[[神人部氏|神人部直]]、[[磯部氏|石辺公]]、[[長国造|長公]]、[[都佐国造|都佐公]]、[[長阿比古氏]]、[[億岐氏]]などがある。 == 始祖 == 『[[古事記]]』では[[大物主|大物主大神]]の[[続柄#玄孫|5世孫]]である[[大田田根子|意富多多泥古]]（オホタタネコ）は神君および[[賀茂朝臣氏|鴨君]]（のちの賀茂朝臣）の祖と記されており、『[[日本書紀]]』でも神代第八段、一書（異伝）に[[大物主神|大三輪神]]の子は甘茂君・三輪君などと記されている。また巻第五に[[崇神天皇]]8年12月条にも、大物主神の子[[大田田根子]]（オホタタネコ）は今の三輪君などの祖であると記述されている。 これら史料から、三輪氏は大物主神の後裔として、その祖神の祭祀を司る有力[[氏族]]であったことがわかる。ただし『[[日本書紀]]』や『[[先代旧事本紀]]』では[[事代主|事代主神]]の子孫も三輪氏となっている。 『[[新撰姓氏録]]』大和国神別の三輪氏は[[スサノオ|素佐能雄命]]の[[十七世神|6世孫]]の[[大国主|大国主神]]の後裔とする。 == 動向 == 『[[日本書紀]]』によれば、[[垂仁天皇]]3年3月[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍]]が来朝したとき、三輪君の祖の[[大三輪大友主]]が遣わされ尋問したという。大友主は[[仲哀天皇]]9年2月、四大夫の一人として[[仲哀天皇]][[崩御]]の宮中を守っている。 [[敏達天皇]]14年（[[585年]]）6月、[[三輪逆]]は排仏派として[[物部守屋]]・[[中臣磐余]]とともに[[寺]]・[[仏塔]]を焼き[[仏像]]を捨てることを企てた。[[用明天皇]]元年（[[586年]]）5月、[[穴穂部皇子]]が[[殯宮]]で炊屋姫皇后（のちの[[推古天皇]]）を[[強姦|犯そうとした]]とき、炊屋姫の寵臣だった三輪逆が[[皇后]]を守った。 [[斉明天皇|皇極天皇]]の時、[[三輪文屋]]は[[山背大兄王]]に仕え、運命をともにしている。 [[大化]]5年（[[649年]]）5月、[[三輪色夫]]が[[新羅]]に派遣されている。 [[天智天皇]]2年（[[663年]]）3月にも[[三輪根麻呂]]が[[新羅]]征討の中将軍に任命されている。 天武天皇元年（[[672年]]）6月、[[伊勢国|伊勢介]][[三輪子首]]は大海人皇子（のちの[[天武天皇]]）を[[鈴鹿郡]]（[[三重県]]鈴鹿郡・[[亀山市]]と[[鈴鹿市]]の一部）に迎え、同年7月には[[三輪高市麻呂]]らが箸陵（[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]箸中）付近で[[近江朝廷|近江朝廷軍]]に大勝した。この[[壬申の乱]]における活躍が天武・持統朝における大三輪氏の[[地位]]を高めた。[[持統天皇]]3年（[[689年]]）2月、[[大神安麻呂]]が判事になる。同6年3月、[[中納言]][[三輪高市麻呂]]は[[天皇]]の[[伊勢国|伊勢]][[行幸]]が農事を妨げるとして再度にわたり[[諫言]]した。 [[中世]]には三輪氏の子孫[[地下人|地下]][[官人]]'''山井家'''（やまのいけ）と称した。[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]に活躍した[[山井景光]]は[[笛]]の名人として知られ、[[後醍醐天皇|後醍醐]]・[[光明天皇|光明]]両[[天皇]]に笛を伝授し、その功績から[[雅楽頭]]を経て[[従五位|従五位上]][[安芸守]]まで昇った{{Sfn|豊永|2004|p=252 - 258}}。 === 三輪氏と対外政策 === 三輪氏やその一族は、古くから対外政策に携わってきた。それは、以下の[[伝承]]から確認できる[[鈴木正信]]『日本古代の氏族と系譜伝承』（[[吉川弘文館]]、[[2017年]]（平成29年））。 * [[垂仁天皇]]3年3月に[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍]]が来朝した際に、三輪君の祖の[[大三輪大友主]]が遣わされた。 * [[神功皇后]]の[[三韓征伐]]の際に[[筑紫国]]に[[大己貴神社]]が祀られた。 * 神功皇后の[[新羅]]征伐の際に従軍した[[大矢田宿禰]]は大三輪真鳥という人物であったとする伝説が存在する。 * [[孝徳天皇]]期以前に[[三輪東人|三輪栗隈君東人]]が[[任那]]と[[百済]]の[[国境]]を視察した。 * [[天武天皇]]13年5月28日に[[三輪引田難波麻呂|三輪引田君難波麻呂]]が[[高句麗]]に遣わされた。 * [[大化]]5年（[[649年]]）5月に[[三輪色夫|三輪君色夫]]が[[新羅]]に派遣されている。 * [[天智天皇]]2年（[[663年]]）3月に[[三輪根麻呂|三輪君根麻呂]]が[[新羅]]征討の中将軍に任命され、それに[[粟鹿神社]]祭主の神部根マロも従軍している。 また、三輪引田君氏の本拠地である[[秉田神社]]（大和国木上郡引田郷）から[[初瀬川 (奈良県)]]を挟んだ対岸には狛という地名があること、『[[新撰姓氏録]]』には「'''狛人野　[[大物主命]]子櫛日方命之後也'''」・「'''神人　[[高句麗|高麗]]国人許利都之後也'''」と見えること、三輪氏は陶邑の須恵器を作成する工人を配下に置き、そこで作られた須恵器を用いて[[三輪山]]で[[祭祀]]を行っていた [[溝口優樹]]『日本古代の地域と社会統合』（吉川弘文館、[[2015年]]（[[平成]]27年）オンデマンド版　ISBN　9784642746182　）ことなどからも、三輪氏と[[朝鮮半島]]の関係は深かったことが推察できる。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Notelist}} {{Reflist|1}} == 参考文献 == * Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[samurai]] family who have served the [[Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[Asuka period]]. During the [[Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Isonokami clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[Silla]]. In the second year of [[Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[samurai]] family who have served the [[Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=draft}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[Asuka period]]. During the [[Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Isonokami clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[Silla]]. In the second year of [[Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=draft}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[Silla]]. In the second year of [[Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[samurai]] family who have served the [[Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[Asuka period]]. During the [[Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Isonokami clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[samurai]] family who have served the [[Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[Asuka period]]. During the [[Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Isonokami clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[Silla]]. In the second year of [[Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Miwa] ]] ]] == Related topics == * [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] * [[Ōtataneko]] * [[Kamo no Asomi clan]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Citation|author=坂本太郎・家永三郎・井上光貞・大野晋|title=[[Nihon Shoki]]|publisher=岩波書店|year=1994}} * {{Citation|author=倉野憲司|title=[[古事記]]|publisher=岩波書店|series=岩波文庫|year=1963}} * {{Citation|author=岩沢愿彦|title=[[系図纂要]]|publisher=名著出版|year=1997}} * {{Cite book|author=太田亮|editor=上田萬年・三上参次|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id=47004572|volume=1|chapter=大神　オホミワ|pages=1308-1313|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1130845/728|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070}} * {{Cite book|author=佐伯有清|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=雄山閣出版|year=1994}} * {{Cite book|author=坂本太郎・平野邦雄|title=日本古代氏族人名辞典|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=1990}} * {{Cite book|author=宝賀寿男|title=古代氏族の研究⑦　三輪氏 大物主神の祭祀者|publisher=青垣出版|year=2015}} * {{Cite journal|author=村島秀次|title=「大物主神 = 事代主神」論|journal=歴史研究|issue=618|year=2014}} * {{Cite journal|author=豊永聡美|title=大神景光-後醍醐・光明天皇の御笛師-|journal=日本音楽史研究|issue=5|year=2004}} (reprinted in {{Cite book|title=中世の天皇と音楽|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=2006|isbn=4642028609}}) * {{Cite web|author=おとくにフォトカルチャーラボ|title=三輪氏考|url=http://ek1010.sakura.ne.jp/1234-7-16.html|accessdate=2023-06-12}} * {{Suwa Faith}}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{translated page|ja|大神氏|version=102530351|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:japanese clans]] }} [[sn:Miwa clan]] [[en:Miwa clan]] [[ja:大神氏]] [[sn:iwa clan]] [[ja:Miwa clan]]

Miwa] ]] ]] == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] * [[Ōtataneko]] * [[Kamo no Asomi clan]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Citation|author=坂本太郎・家永三郎・井上光貞・大野晋|title=[[Nihon Shoki]]|publisher=岩波書店|year=1994}} * {{Citation|author=倉野憲司|title=[[古事記]]|publisher=岩波書店|series=岩波文庫|year=1963}} * {{Citation|author=岩沢愿彦|title=[[系図纂要]]|publisher=名著出版|year=1997}} * {{Cite book|author=太田亮|editor=上田萬年・三上参次|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id=47004572|volume=1|chapter=大神　オホミワ|pages=1308-1313|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1130845/728|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070}} * {{Cite book|author=佐伯有清|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=雄山閣出版|year=1994}} * {{Cite book|author=坂本太郎・平野邦雄|title=日本古代氏族人名辞典|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=1990}} * {{Cite book|author=宝賀寿男|title=古代氏族の研究⑦　三輪氏 大物主神の祭祀者|publisher=青垣出版|year=2015}} * {{Cite journal|author=村島秀次|title=「大物主神 = 事代主神」論|journal=歴史研究|issue=618|year=2014}} * {{Cite journal|author=豊永聡美|title=大神景光-後醍醐・光明天皇の御笛師-|journal=日本音楽史研究|issue=5|year=2004}} (reprinted in {{Cite book|title=中世の天皇と音楽|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=2006|isbn=4642028609}}) * {{Cite web|author=おとくにフォトカルチャーラボ|title=三輪氏考|url=http://ek1010.sakura.ne.jp/1234-7-16.html|accessdate=2023-06-12}} * {{Suwa Faith}}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} {{translated page|ja|大神氏|version=102530351|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:japanese clans]] }} [[sn:Miwa clan]] [[en:Miwa clan]] [[ja:大神氏]] [[sn:iwa clan]] [[ja:Miwa clan]]

{{Short description|Japanese social class and samurai clan}} {{Distinguish|text=[[Suwa clan]] a medieval Japanese clan which may be descended from it}} {{notability|date=January 2023}} {{Infobox Japanese clan|home province=[[Yamato Province]]|founder={{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}(legendary)
Historically unknown|cadet branches=|surname nihongo=大神|surname=Miwa|image=三本杉紋.jpg|parent house=[[Kamo clan]]}}{{Infobox Japanese clan | name = Miwa clan → Ōmiwa clan | image = [[File:三本杉（さんぼんすぎ）.png|250px]]
Representative crest: Three Cedars (Sanbon-sugi) | home_province = Yamato Province | titles = Kimi
Ōmiwa Kimi → later Ōmiwa Asomi | founder = Ōhiko
(descendant of Ōmononushi) | current_head = | founding_year = | dissolution = | cadet_branches = Yamanoi family (Chikage)
Fujibayashi family (Chikage)
Ōtsu family (Chikage)
Takamiyagawa family (Shakage)
Tsutsui clan (Warrior clan)
Anan clan (Warrior clan)
Tajiri clan (Warrior clan)
Mitsuyoshi clan (Warrior clan)
Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[samurai]] family who have served the [[Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[Asuka period]]. During the [[Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Isonokami clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[Silla]]. In the second year of [[Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Miwa] ]] ]] == See Also == * [[Ōmiwa Shrine]] * [[Ōtataneko]] * [[Kamo no Asomi clan]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Citation|author=坂本太郎・家永三郎・井上光貞・大野晋|title=[[Nihon Shoki]]|publisher=岩波書店|year=1994}} * {{Citation|author=倉野憲司|title=[[古事記]]|publisher=岩波書店|series=岩波文庫|year=1963}} * {{Citation|author=岩沢愿彦|title=[[系図纂要]]|publisher=名著出版|year=1997}} * {{Cite book|author=太田亮|editor=上田萬年・三上参次|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id=47004572|volume=1|chapter=大神　オホミワ|pages=1308-1313|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1130845/728|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070}} * {{Cite book|author=佐伯有清|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=雄山閣出版|year=1994}} * {{Cite book|author=坂本太郎・平野邦雄|title=日本古代氏族人名辞典|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=1990}} * {{Cite book|author=宝賀寿男|title=古代氏族の研究⑦　三輪氏 大物主神の祭祀者|publisher=青垣出版|year=2015}} * {{Cite journal|author=村島秀次|title=「大物主神 = 事代主神」論|journal=歴史研究|issue=618|year=2014}} * {{Cite journal|author=豊永聡美|title=大神景光-後醍醐・光明天皇の御笛師-|journal=日本音楽史研究|issue=5|year=2004}} (reprinted in {{Cite book|title=中世の天皇と音楽|publisher=吉川弘文館|year=2006|isbn=4642028609}}) * {{Cite web|author=おとくにフォトカルチャーラボ|title=三輪氏考|url=http://ek1010.sakura.ne.jp/1234-7-16.html|accessdate=2023-06-12}} * {{Suwa Faith}}{{Miwa and Yamato Faith}} [[Category:translated pages without meta categories]]\n{{translated page|ja|大神氏|version=102530351|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:japanese clans]] }} [[sn:Miwa clan]] [[en:Miwa clan]] [[ja:大神氏]] [[sn:iwa clan]] [[ja:Miwa clan]]

LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|qq=draft}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. (descendant of Ōmononushi) | current_head = | founding_year = | dissolution = | cadet_branches = Yamanoi family (Chikage)
