The ''[[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[:en:Emperor Yōmei|Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[:en:Taika era|Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[:en:Silla|Silla]]. In the second year of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[:en:Prince Ōama|Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[:en:Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[:en:Medieval period|Medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[:en:Emperor Go-Daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[:en:Emperor Kōmyō|Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[:en:Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[:en:Samurai|Samurai]] family who have served the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[:en:Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[:en:Tenri City|Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]]. During the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Mononobe clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[:en:Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[:en:Samurai|Samurai]] family who have served the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[:en:Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[:en:Tenri City|Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]]. During the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Mononobe clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[:en:Sendai Kuji Hongi|Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[:en:Emperor Yōmei|Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[:en:Taika era|Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[:en:Silla|Silla]]. In the second year of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[:en:Prince Ōama|Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[:en:Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[:en:Medieval period|Medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[:en:Emperor Go-Daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[:en:Emperor Kōmyō|Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. The ''[[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[:en:Emperor Yōmei|Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[:en:Taika era|Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[:en:Silla|Silla]]. In the second year of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[:en:Prince Ōama|Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[:en:Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[:en:Medieval period|Medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[:en:Emperor Go-Daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[:en:Emperor Kōmyō|Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[:en:Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[:en:Samurai|Samurai]] family who have served the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[:en:Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[:en:Tenri City|Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]]. During the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Mononobe clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[:en:Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[:en:Samurai|Samurai]] family who have served the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[:en:Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[:en:Tenri City|Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]]. During the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Mononobe clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[:en:Sendai Kuji Hongi|Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[:en:Emperor Yōmei|Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[:en:Taika era|Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[:en:Silla|Silla]]. In the second year of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[:en:Prince Ōama|Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[:en:Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[:en:Medieval period|Medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[:en:Emperor Go-Daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[:en:Emperor Kōmyō|Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Miwa]]] == See Also == * [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] * [[Ōtataneko]] * [[Kamo no Asomi clan]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * During the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Mononobe clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[:en:Sendai Kuji Hongi|Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[:en:Emperor Yōmei|Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[:en:Taika era|Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[:en:Silla|Silla]]. In the second year of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[:en:Prince Ōama|Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[:en:Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[:en:Medieval period|Medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[:en:Emperor Go-Daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[:en:Emperor Kōmyō|Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. In the 8th year of the reign of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Miwa]]] == See Also == * [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] * [[Ōtataneko]] * [[Kamo no Asomi clan]] == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[:en:Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[:en:Samurai|Samurai]] family who have served the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[:en:Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[:en:Tenri City|Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. In the 8th year of the reign of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Temmu]], the Miwa clan was renamed Miwa-no-kun and given the surname Ogami-chosin.{{clarify|date=March 2023}} The descendants of Koichi Maro's son Shinobito{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served as the Ogami High Priestess. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt. Wakita clan (Warrior clan) }} The '''Ōmiwa clan''' (おおみわうじ), also known as the '''Miwa clan''' (みわうじ), is a clan originating from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]], with the deity [[Ōmononushi]] as its ancestral god. == Overview == The '''{{nihongo|Miwa clan|大神氏|Miwa-uji}}''' is a Japanese ''[[:en:Shake (social class)|shake]]'' and [[:en:Samurai|Samurai]] family who have served the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Miwa Shrine]] for generations. The ancestor of the Miwa family is said to be [[Ōkuninushi|Okuninushi no Mikoto]], via {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}. The Omiwa clan, also known as the '''Ogami clan''', were a prominent family in ancient Japan known for their responsibility in performing state rituals for the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Court]]. The clan rose to prominence in the period between the latter half of the 5th century and the 6th century, before the establishment of capital cities such as [[Heijō-kyō|Heijo-kyo]] and [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian-kyo]]. The clan's main center of influence was the area around [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mt. Miwa]], which was considered a significant religious and political site. According to tradition, the ancestors of the Ogami clan were able to calm the first epidemic in Japan and this belief has been passed down through the generations to the present-day [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]. Recent research has shed light on the role and significance of the Ogami clan in ancient royal power and rituals. == Overview == The direct ancestor of the clan is Ōhiko, the grandson of [[Ōtataneko]]. The Ōmiwa clan venerates the [[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]] located in Miwa, Sakurai City, Nara Prefecture. The clan's base was in the Shiki area of Yamato Province, encompassing parts of modern-day [[:en:Shiki District, Nara|Shiki District]] and parts of [[:en:Tenri City|Tenri City]] and western [[Sakurai City]]. The clan's name is derived from the locality of Ōmiwa in Yamato Province. Initially, the clan's title was '''Kimi''', but in the 13th year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (684), members of the clan, including [[Miwa Takachi Maro]], were granted the Ōmiwa surname[[Miwa clan#otokuni|Three Cedars Study]]. The clan held the highest Rank among the clans in the late [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]]. During the [[:en:Nara period|Nara period]], many members started using the surname Miwa[[Miwa clan#kodai|『Encyclopedia of Ancient Japanese Clans』]]. Related clans include [[Kamo no Asomi clan|Kamo no Kimi]], [[Kannabe no Ason clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Kannabe clan|Kannabe no Ason]], [[Mononobe clan|Isonokami no Kimi]], [[Nagakuni clan|Nagakuni no Kimi]], [[Tsukasa clan|Tsukasa no Kimi]], [[Nagahiko clan|Nagahiko no Kimi]], and [[Oki clan|Oki no Kimi]]. == Founder == According to the ''[[Kojiki]]'', Ōtataneko (Ohotataneko), the fifth-generation descendant of Ōmononushi, is the ancestor of both the Miwa and Kamo clans. The ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' also mentions that the god Ōmononushi had children who founded several clans, including the Miwa and Kamo clans. Additionally, the ''[[:en:Sendai Kuji Hongi|Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'' states that both the Miwa and Kamo clans are descendants of Ōmononushi. The ''[[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]]'' lists the Miwa clan under the ''Shinbetsu'' (descendants of gods) Category, identifying them as descendants of Ōkuninushi, the sixth-generation descendant of Susanoo. == Activities == According to the ''Nihon Shoki'', when [[Amenohiboko]] arrived in Japan during the third year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]]'s reign, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. In the ninth year of [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Emperor Chūai]]'s reign, Ōtomonushi was one of the four daibu guarding the palace where Emperor Chūai had died. In the 14th year of [[Emperor Bidatsu]]'s reign (585), [[Miwa Saka]] joined forces with anti-Buddhist factions to burn temples and discard Buddhist images. In the first year of [[:en:Emperor Yōmei|Emperor Yōmei]]'s reign (586), Miwa Saka defended [[:en:Empress Suiko|Empress Suiko]] when [[Prince Anahobe]] attempted to assault her at her burial palace. During the reign of [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]], [[Miwa Bun'ya]] served [[Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], sharing his fate. In the fifth year of the [[:en:Taika era|Taika era]] (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was dispatched to [[:en:Silla|Silla]]. In the second year of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]'s reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla. During the first year of [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]]'s reign (672), [[Miwa Koshikubi]] greeted [[:en:Prince Ōama|Prince Ōama]] (later Emperor Tenmu) at [[Suzuka District]] (present-day Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture). In July of the same year, [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] and others achieved a significant victory against the [[Ōmi Court]] army near [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]] in Sakurai City. These accomplishments during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]] elevated the status of the Ōmiwa clan during the reigns of Emperor Tenmu and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]. In the third year of Empress Jitō's reign (689), [[Ōmiwa no Yasumaro]] became a judge. In the sixth year, [[:en:Minister of the Interior|Chūnagon]] [[Miwa Takachi Maro]] repeatedly advised the Emperor that her pilgrimage to [[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]] hindered agricultural activities. During the [[:en:Medieval period|Medieval period]], the descendants of the Miwa clan referred to themselves as the Yamanoi family, serving as low-Ranking officials. In the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]], [[Yamanoi Kagemitsu]] became renowned as a master of the flute, instructing both [[:en:Emperor Go-Daigo|Emperor Go-Daigo]] and [[:en:Emperor Kōmyō|Emperor Kōmyō]] and eventually rising to the position of head of the court musicians with the Rank of Senior Fifth Rank Upper and Governor of Aki ProvinceSuzuki Masanobu "Study on Ancient Japanese Clans: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. === Ōmiwa clan and foreign policy === The Ōmiwa clan and its related clans have been involved in foreign policy since ancient times. This is evident from the following legends and historical eventsSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017: * In the third year of Emperor Suinin's reign, when Amenohiboko came to Japan, [[Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi]] was dispatched to interrogate him. * During Empress Jingū's conquest of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, the Ōmiwa clan enshrined Ōnamuchi Shrine in Tsukushi Province. * During Empress Jingū's expedition against Silla, a legend states that [[Ōmiwa no Matari]], also known as Ōyadano Sukune, participated. * Before Emperor Kōtoku's reign, [[Miwa Kurikuma no Kimi Azuma]] was sent to inspect the borders of Mimana and Baekje. * On May 28th, the 13th year of Emperor Tenmu's reign, [[Miwa Hikida no Kimi Namimaro]] was dispatched to Goguryeo. * In the fifth year of the Taika era (649), [[Miwa Irofu]] was sent to Silla. * In the second year of Emperor Tenji's reign (663), [[Miwa Nemaro]] was appointed as the general for an expedition against Silla, accompanied by the priestly head of [[Awaga Shrine]], Kamube Nemaro. The Miwa Hikida clan's stronghold was located across the [[Hatsuse River]] from the place known as "Koma" (狛). According to the ''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', the Komano clan descended from the deities [[Ōkuninushi]] and [[Ōmononushi]]. It is also noted that the Miwa clan had potters creating sue ware used in the rituals at [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]][[Mizoguchi Yūki]] "Japan's Ancient Regions and Social Integration", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015. These connections indicate a deep relationship between the Miwa clan and the Korean PeninsulaSuzuki Masanobu "Japanese Ancient Clan Studies: Miwa Clan", Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2017. == History == During an epidemic in Japan [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]] was given guidance in the form of a dream to seek out a man named {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}|太田田根子}} and appoint him as head priest.{{cite book |author=Aston, William George. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2 |date=1896 |publisher=The Japan Society London |isbn=9780524053478 |pages=150–164 |author-link=William George Aston}} He eventually found him in [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo Province]].{{Cite journal |last=Ellwood |first=Robert S. |date=1990 |title=The Sujin Religious Revolution |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=17 |issue=2/3 |pages=199–217 |doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217 |jstor=30234018 |issn=0304-1042|doi-access=free }} When he was found and installed, the pestilence eventually subsided, allowing five cereal crops to ripen. Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|Ikagashikoo|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko ... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}} To this day the [[Miwa clan|Miwa sept]] of the [[Kamo clan]] claim to be descents from {{ill|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|1=Ōtataneko|4=fr|5=Ōtataneko命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtataneko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to FR}}, while Ikagashikoo was a claimed ancestor of the now extinct [[Mononobe clan]]. According to notes in the genealogy, the Daiminushi family{{clarify|date=March 2023}} served the [[Southern Court]] during the period of the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-cho period]]. Many members of the family died in the civil wars between the Northern and Southern dynasties. After the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the legitimate lineage served as high priests, but some of the family members became warriors and served the Miyoshi and [[Kitabatake clan|Kitabatake clans]]. After the Hobo break,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} the Daikami family took the name Takamiya and served the Ogami Shrine, and their descendants continued to serve the shrine until the [[Meiji Restoration]]. One branch of the Miwa family, known as the Hiyoshi, served the [[Usa Jingū]] in ancient times. Their descendants served as the chief priest of the Usa Jingu for a long time until they were replaced by the Usa clan. From their descendants, medieval warriors such as Ogata, Ono, and Anan were born,{{clarify|date=March 2023}} and during the [[:en:Sengoku period|Sengoku period]], they played a part in the military power of the [[:en:Ōtomo clan|Otomo clan]], the feudal lords in [[Kyushu]]. ==Ancestry== {{Eight generations of Izumo}} == Further reading == * [https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315617909/clans-religion-ancient-japan-masanobu-suzuki Clans and Religion in Ancient Japan The mythology of Mt.
